what: The heuristic extracts depot, customer, visited, and location facts from semantic fact names, then reconstructs the routing-cost matrix from grounded `visit` and `return-to-depot` operator costs. At evaluation it identifies the current location and unvisited customers. It computes an MST/degree-relaxation routing lower bound and a nearest-neighbor completion ending at the depot. When exact, non-folded capacity and demand PNEs are available, the greedy completion respects the current load and inserts depot route breaks; it also detects aggregate vehicle-limit infeasibility when exact max-vehicle data is available. The final estimate is the maximum of the structural lower bound and 90% of the greedy completion.
why: CVRP states are naturally characterized by the current endpoint and remaining customer set, while all routing costs can be recovered robustly from grounded operators without parsing fragile derived PNE names. MST and degree relaxations are inexpensive and stable, whereas a discounted greedy completion provides stronger route-ordering guidance for the small-to-medium customer sets represented here. Capacity-aware route breaks are especially valuable in the many-small-capacity instances, but the implementation safely degrades to pure routing guidance when the translator folds away capacity or demand variables.
